Algorithmic game theory (AGT) is an interdisciplinary field at the intersection of [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) and [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science), focused on understanding and designing algorithms for environments where multiple strategic agents interact.
Almost Ideal Demand System (AIDS) is a consumer demand model used primarily by economists to study [consumer behavior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_behaviour).
ambiguity aversion (also known as uncertainty aversion) is a preference for known risks over unknown risks.

analytic narrative is a [social science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_science) research method seeking to combine historical narratives with the rigor of [rational choice theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rational_choice_theory), particularly through the use of [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory).

definition: Competition law is the field of [law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law) that promotes or seeks to maintain [market competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_competition) by regulating [anti-competitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-competitive) conduct by companies.
Competitive altruism is a possible mechanism for the persistence of [cooperative behaviours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperation), specifically those that are performed unconditionally.
complete contract is an important concept from [contract theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contract_theory).
complete information is an economic situation or game in which knowledge about other market participants or players is available to all participants.
complete mixing refers to a modeling assumption where each individual in a population has an equal probability of interacting with any other individual.

Compositional game theory is a branch of [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) and [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science), which aims to present large complex games as a composition of simple small games.
compromise is to make a deal between different parties where each party gives up part of their [demand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demand).
concave game is a generalization of the [normal-form game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal-form_game) defined by Rosen.
Conflict escalation is the process by which conflicts grow in severity or scale over time.
Congestion games (CG) are a class of games in [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory).
conjectural variation is the belief that one firm has an idea about the way its competitors may react if it varies its output or price.

Consideration set is a model used in [consumer behaviour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_behaviour) to represent all of the brands and products a consumer evaluates before making a final purchase decision.

consumer choice is the branch of [microeconomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microeconomics) that relates [preferences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preference_(economics)) to consumption expenditures and to [consumer demand curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supply_and_demand).

Consumer sovereignty is the [economic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics) concept that the consumer has some controlling power over goods that are produced, and that the consumer is the best judge of their own welfare.
Consumer value is used to describe a consumer's strong relative preference for certain subjectively evaluated product or service attributes.

Consumption smoothing is an [economic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic) concept for the practice of optimizing a person's [standard of living](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_of_living) through an appropriate balance between savings and consumption over time.

contingent cooperator is a person or agent who is willing to act in the collective interest, rather than his short-term selfish interest, if he observes a majority of the other agents in the collective doing the same.

continuous game is a mathematical concept, used in [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory), that generalizes the idea of an ordinary game like [tic-tac-toe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tic-tac-toe) (noughts and crosses) or checkers (draughts).
cooperative or coalitional game is a [game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game) with groups of [players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_(game)) who form binding 2012.

coco value (short for cooperative–competitive value) is a [solution concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solution_concept) in [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) for two-player [normal-form game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal-form_game)s with [transferable utility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transferable_utility).

Copenhagen Consensus is a project that seeks to establish priorities for advancing global welfare using methodologies based on the theory of [welfare economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_economics), using [cost–benefit analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cost–benefit_analysis).

core is the [set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_(mathematics)) of [feasible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feasible_region) allocations or [imputations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imputation_(game_theory)) where no coalition of agents can benefit by breaking away from the grand coalition.

cornering the market consists of obtaining sufficient control of a particular [stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock), [commodity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commodity), [human capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_capital) or other [asset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asset) in an attempt to reduce [competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Competition_(economics)).

correlated equilibrium is a [solution concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solution_concept) that is more general than the well known [Nash equilibrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash_equilibrium).

cost of living is the [cost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cost) of maintaining a certain [standard of living](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_of_living) for an individual or a [household](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Household).
Cost–benefit analysis (CBA), sometimes also called benefit–cost analysis, is a systematic approach to estimating the strengths and weaknesses of alternatives.
Countersignaling is the behavior in which agents with the highest level of a given property invest less into proving it than individuals with a medium level of the same property.
Cram is a [mathematical game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_game) played on a sheet of [graph paper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_paper) (or any type of grid).

Cultural group selection is an explanatory model within [cultural evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_evolution) of how cultural traits evolve according to the competitive advantage they bestow upon a group.

cursed equilibrium is a [solution concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solution_concept) for [static game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Static_game)s of [incomplete information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayesian_game).
De-escalation refers to the methods and actions taken to decrease the severity of a [conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conflict_(process)), whether of physical, verbal or another nature.

deadweight loss is the loss of societal [economic welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_welfare) due to production/consumption of a good at a quantity where [marginal benefit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marginal_benefit) (to society) does not equal [marginal cost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marginal_cost) (to society).
demand is the quantity of a [good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goods) that consumers are willing and able to purchase at various prices during a given time.
Deregulation is the process of removing or reducing state regulations, typically in the economic sphere.

Deterrence theory refers to the scholarship and practice of how threats of using force by one party can convince another party to refrain from initiating some other course of action.

Dialogical logic (, also known as the logic of dialogues) is a pragmatic approach to the [semantics of logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantics_of_logic) developed in the 1950s by [Paul Lorenzen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Lorenzen) and [Kuno Lorenz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuno_Lorenz).

durapolist or [durable good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durable_good) monopolist is a producer that manipulates the [durability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durable_goods) of its product.

epsilon-equilibrium, or near-Nash equilibrium, is a [strategy profile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_profile) that approximately satisfies the condition of [Nash equilibrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash_equilibrium).

evolutionarily stable strategy (ESS) is a [strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_(game_theory)) (or set of strategies) that is impermeable when adopted by a [population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_genetics) in adaptation to a specific environment, that is to say it cannot be displaced by an alternative strategy (or set of strategies) which may be novel or initially rare.
evolutionary attractor is a point in an evolutionary space where a selection process will always drive trait values towards that point from the region around it.

Evolutionary dynamics is a branch of mathematical evolutionary biology that developed from research using [differential equations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Differential_equations) to model both [genetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetics) and [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotype) change.
Evolutionary economics is a school of [economic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics) thought that is inspired by [evolutionary biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_biology).
Evolutionary game theory (EGT) is the application of [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) to evolving populations in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology).
excess burden of [taxation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxation) is one of the economic losses that society suffers as the result of taxes or subsidies.

expected utility hypothesis is a foundational assumption in [mathematical economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_economics) concerning [decision making](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_theory) under [uncertainty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncertainty).

expenditure minimization problem is the [dual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duality_(optimization)) of the [utility maximization problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utility_maximization_problem): then the demand is a [[1:1 correspondence|correspondence]], and not a function.

Explore Then Commit (ETC) is an algorithm for the [multi-armed bandit problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-armed_bandit) foc,used on finding the best trade-off between exploration and exploitation.

Extended sympathy in [welfare economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_economics) refers to interpersonal value judgments of the form that social state x for person A is ranked better than, worse than, or as good as social state y for person B (Arrow, 1963, pp.
externality is a cost or benefit to an uninvolved third party that arises as an effect of another party's (or parties') activity.

Fair division is an optimisation problem in [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) of dividing a set of [resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resources) among several parties who have an [entitlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entitlement_(fair_division)) to them so that each party receives their due share.
false economy or hallucinated economy is an action that does save money at the beginning but which, over a longer period of time, results in more money being spent or wasted than being saved.

feasibility condition is a fundamental concept in [microeconomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microeconomics) used in conjunction with the tangency condition to solve the [consumer choice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consumer_choice) problem and derive the [demand function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demand_function).

Fei–Ranis model of economic growth is a dualism model in [developmental economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Development_economics) or [welfare economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_economics) that has been developed by [[John C.
Fibonacci nim is a mathematical [subtraction game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subtraction_game), a variant of the game of [nim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nim).

fictitious play is a [learning rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learning_rule) that describes how players might learn over time in repeated [strategic interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_interaction)s.
first-order approach is a simplifying assumption used to solve models with a [principal-agent problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal-agent_problem).

Fisher's principle is an [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution)ary model that explains why the [sex ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_ratio) of most [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) that produce [offspring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offspring) through [sexual reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_reproduction) is approximately 1:1 between [male](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male)s and [female](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female)s.
focal point (or Schelling point) is a solution that people tend to choose by default in the absence of communication in order to avoid [[Coordination game#Experimental results|coordination failure]].

folk theorems are a class of theorems describing an abundance of [Nash equilibrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash_equilibrium) payoff profiles in [repeated games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repeated_game) .

free entry is a condition in which [[:wikt:firm|firms]] can freely enter the [market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_(economics)) for an [economic good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_good) by establishing production and beginning to sell the product.

Game design is the process of creating and shaping the mechanics, systems, rules, and gameplay of a [game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game).
game form, game frame, ruleset, or outcome function is the set of [rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_rule) that govern a game and determine its outcome based on each player's choices.

Game semantics is an approach to [formal semantics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_semantics_(logic)) that grounds the concepts of [truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truth) or [validity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Validity_(logic)) on [game-theoretic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) concepts, such as the existence of a [winning strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winning_strategy) for a player.
Game theory is the study of [mathematical model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_model)s of strategic interactions.
Game theory on networks is a field that studies strategy in competing interest interactions among rational or adaptive players that are affected by the topology of networks.

game tree is a graph representing all possible game states within a [sequential game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sequential_game) that has [perfect information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_information).
generalized game is a game or puzzle that has been generalized so that it can be played on a board or grid of any size.

Generational imbalance is the economic and political tension which characterizes a state which has a reduced birth rate and increased health resulting in an increasing aging population compared to its younger working population; cost and generosity of welfare systems also plays a role.

Genuine progress indicator (GPI) is a [metric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance_metric) that has been suggested to replace, or supplement, [gross domestic product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product) (GDP).

genus theory in [impartial game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impartial_game)s is a theory by which some games played under the [misère play convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misère_play_convention) can be analysed, to predict the [outcome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outcome_(game_theory)) class of games.

Ghent system is the name given to an arrangement in some countries whereby the main responsibility for [welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_spending) payments, especially [unemployment benefits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment_benefits), is held by [trade union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_union)s rather than a [government agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_agency).
Gibbs lemma is a result that is useful in maximization problems.

gift-exchange game, also commonly known as the gift exchange dilemma, is a common economic [game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) introduced by [George Akerlof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Akerlof) and [Janet Yellen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Yellen) to model reciprocacy in labor relations.

Herfindahl index (also known as Herfindahl–Hirschman Index, HHI, or sometimes HHI-score) is a measure of the size of [firms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporation) in relation to the [industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industry_(economics)) they are in and is an indicator of the amount of competition among them.

hidden welfare state is a term coined by [Christopher Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Howard_(professor)), professor of government at the [College of William and Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_William_and_Mary), to refer to tax expenditures with social welfare objectives that are often not included in discussions about the U.S.

Hobbesian trap (or Schelling's dilemma) is a [theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theory) that explains why [preemptive strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preemptive_strike)s occur between two groups, out of bilateral [fear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear) of an imminent [attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offensive_(military)).

homicidal chauffeur problem is a mathematical [pursuit problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pursuit-evasion) which pits a hypothetical runner, who can only move slowly, but is highly maneuverable, against the driver of a motor vehicle, which is much faster but far less maneuverable, who is attempting to run him down.

Homo economicus, or economic man, is the portrayal of humans as [agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agency_(philosophy)) who are consistently [rational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rationality) and narrowly [self-interested](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rational_egoism), and who pursue their subjectively defined ends [optimally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimal_decision).
Hoover index, also known as the Robin Hood index or the Schutz index, is a measure of [income inequality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_inequality).

Horizontal integration is the process of a [company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Company) increasing [production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production_(economics)) of goods or services at the same level of the [value chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Value_chain), in the same industry.
hot game is one in which each player can improve their position by making the next move.

Human Poverty Index (HPI) was an indication of the poverty of community in a country, developed by the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations) to complement the [Human Development Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index) (HDI) and was first reported as part of the Human Development Report in 1997.

impartial game is a [game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_game) in which the allowable moves depend only on the position and not on which of the two players is currently moving, and where the payoffs are symmetric.

Implementation theory is an area of research in [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) concerned with whether a class of [mechanisms (or institutions) can be designed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanism_design) whose equilibrium outcomes implement a given set of [normative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normative) goals or [welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_economics) criteria.
Incentives are anything that persuade a person or organization to alter their behavior to produce a desired outcome.

Income deficit is the difference between a single person or family's [income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income) and its [poverty threshold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_threshold) or poverty line, when the former is exceeded by the latter.

Income inequality metrics or income distribution metrics are used by social scientists to measure the [distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distribution_of_wealth) of [income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income) and [economic inequality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_inequality) among the participants in a particular economy, such as that of a specific country or of the world in general.

income-consumption curve (also called income expansion path and income offer curve) is a curve in a graph in which the quantities of two goods are plotted on the two axes; the curve is the [locus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locus_(mathematics)) of points showing the consumption bundles chosen at each of various levels of income.
incomplete contract is one that is defective or uncertain in a material respect.

indistinguishability quotient is a [commutative monoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commutative_monoid) that generalizes and localizes the [Sprague–Grundy theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprague–Grundy_theorem) for a specific game's rule set.

Induction puzzles are [logic puzzle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic_puzzle)s, which are examples of [multi-agent reasoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_epistemic_logic), where the solution evolves along with the principle of [induction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_induction).
Inequity aversion (IA) is the [preference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_preference) for fairness and resistance to incidental inequalities.

Infinite chess is any [variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_variant) of the game of [chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess) played on an [unbounded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounded_set) [chessboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chessboard).

information set is the basis for decision making in a game, which includes the actions available to players and the potential outcomes of each action.

Installed base of a product is the number of units that are currently in use by customers.

mean payoff game is a [zero-sum game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zero-sum_game) played on the vertices of a weighted [directed graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_graph).
Mean-field game theory is the study of strategic decision making by small interacting [agents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agent_(economics)) in very large populations.

means test is a determination of whether an individual or family is eligible for government benefits, assistance or [welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_spending), based upon whether the individual or family possesses the means to do with less or none of that help.

Black's median voter theorem says that if voters and candidates are distributed along a one-dimensional [political spectrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_spectrum), any [Condorcet consistent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condorcet_criterion) voting method will elect the candidate preferred by the [median](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Median) voter.
Mertens stability is a [solution concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solution_concept) used to predict the outcome of a [non-cooperative game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-cooperative_game).
Meshulam's game is a game used to explain a theorem of Roy Meshulam .

mex (minimum excluded value) of a [subset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subset) of a [well-ordered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well-ordered) set is the smallest value from the whole set that does not belong to the subset.

Microeconomics is a branch of [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics) that studies the behavior of individuals and [firms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theory_of_the_firm) in making decisions regarding the allocation of [scarce resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarcity) and the interactions among these individuals and firms.
Microfoundations are an effort to understand macroeconomic phenomena in terms of individual agents' economic behavior and interactions.

minimum effort game or weakest link game is a game in which each person decides how much effort to put in and is rewarded based on the least amount of effort anyone puts in.

missing market is a situation in [microeconomics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microeconomics) where a competitive [market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_(economics)) allowing the [exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade) of a [commodity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commodity) would be [Pareto-efficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pareto-efficient), but no such market exists.

mixed economy is an [economic system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_system) that includes both elements associated with [capitalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitalism), such as [private businesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privately_held_company), and with [socialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialism), such as [nationalized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalization) [government services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_service).
monopoly (from [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) and ) is a market in which one person or company is the only supplier of a particular good or service.

multi-stage game is a sequence of several [simultaneous game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simultaneous_game)s played one after the other.

Mutual knowledge is a fundamental concept about information in [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory), (epistemic) [logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic), and [epistemology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistemology).
n-player game is a game which is well defined for any number of players.
Nanoeconomics is defined as the [economic theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_theory) of single transactions.

Nash equilibrium is a situation where no player could gain more by changing their own [strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_(game_theory)) (holding all other players' strategies fixed) in a game.

national income and product accounts (NIPA) are part of the [national accounts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_accounts) of the United States.

negotiation theory are [decision analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decision_analysis), [behavioral decision-making](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behavioralist_psychology), [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory), and [negotiation analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negotiation).

spite is a phenomenon that occurs when a player's value of an allocation decreases when one or more other players' valuation increases.

Stackelberg leadership model is a [strategic game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategy_game) in [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics) in which the leader firm moves first and then the follower firms move sequentially (hence, it is sometimes described as the leader-follower game).

move, action, or play is any one of the options which a player can choose in a setting where the optimal outcome depends not only on their own actions but also on the actions of others.

strictly determined game is a game where the optimal strategy for each player does not depend on the strategy chosen by the other players.

strong Nash equilibrium (SNE) is a combination of actions of the different players, in which no coalition of players can cooperatively deviate in a way that strictly benefits all of its members, given that the actions of the other players remain fixed.

Structural adjustment programs (SAPs) consist of loans (structural adjustment loans; SALs) provided by the [International Monetary Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund) (IMF) and the [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank) (WB) to countries that experience economic crises.

Student financial aid in Finland consists of government payments (through [Kela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kela_(Finnish_institution))) that provide [economic security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_security) to students and enable all students to study.

subgame perfect equilibrium (SPE), or subgame perfect Nash equilibrium (SPNE), is a [refinement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solution_concept) of the [Nash equilibrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash_equilibrium) concept, specifically designed for [dynamic game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamic_game)s where players make sequential decisions.
substitute goods are two goods that can be used for the same purpose by consumers.

surplus procedure (SP) is a [fair division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_division) protocol for cutting cake in a way that achieves proportional [equitability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equity_(economics)) between 2 people.

surreal number system is a [totally ordered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_order) [proper class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proper_class) containing not only the [real number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_number)s but also [infinite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinity) and [infinitesimal numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infinitesimal), respectively larger or smaller in [absolute value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_value) than any positive real number.
Swap regret is a concept from online learning and [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory).

swing producer or swing supplier is a supplier or a close [oligopolistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oligopoly) group of suppliers of any [commodity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commodity), controlling its global deposits and possessing large spare production capacity.
symmetric game is a game where the payoffs for playing a particular strategy depend only on the other strategies employed, not on who is playing them.
Tacit collusion is a [collusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collusion) between competitors who do not explicitly exchange information but achieve an agreement about coordination of conduct.

terminal investment hypothesis is the idea in [life history theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_history_theory) that as an organism's residual [reproductive value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_value_(population_genetics)) (or the total reproductive value minus the reproductive value of the current breeding attempt) decreases, its reproductive effort will increase.

Theil index is a statistic primarily used to measure [economic inequality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_inequality) package which allows for computation of a variety of inequality indices including Gini, Atkinson, Theil.
threshold population is the minimum number of people needed for a [service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_(economics)) to be worthwhile.

Top trading cycle (TTC) is an algorithm for trading indivisible items without using money.

topological game is an infinite game of [perfect information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_information) played between two players on a [topological space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Topological_space).

definition: Transferable utility is a concept in [cooperative game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperative_game_theory) and in [economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economics).

trembling hand perfect equilibrium, or simply perfect equilibrium, is a type of refinement of a [Nash equilibrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nash_equilibrium) that was first proposed by [Reinhard Selten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinhard_Selten).

Two-level game theory is a [political model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_theory), derived from [game theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory), that illustrates the domestic-international interactions between states.
two-player game is a [multiplayer game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplayer_game) that is played by precisely two players.

Unconditional cash transfer (UCT) programs are [philanthropic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philanthropic) programs that aim to reduce [poverty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty) by providing [financial welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_(financial_aid)) without any conditions upon the receivers' actions.
uncorrelated asymmetry is an arbitrary distinguishing feature between players in an otherwise [symmetric game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetric_game).
Uneconomic growth is [economic growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_growth) that reflects or creates a decline in the [quality of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quality_of_life).

utility–possibility frontier (or utility possibilities curve), is a widely used concept analogous to the better-known [production–possibility frontier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production–possibility_frontier).
value of a statistical life (VSL) is an economic [value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Value_theory) used to quantify the benefit of avoiding a fatality.

Veblen good is a type of [luxury good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxury_good) for which the demand increases as the price increases, in apparent contradiction of the [law of demand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_demand), resulting in an upward-sloping demand curve.

vertical integration, also referred to as vertical consolidation, is an arrangement in which the [supply chain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supply_chain) of a company is integrated and owned by that company.

Waldegrave problem is a problem first described in the second edition of [Pierre Raymond de Montmort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Raymond_de_Montmort)`s [Essay d'analyse sur les jeux de hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Essay_d'analyse_sur_les_jeux_de_hazard), which is the first discussion of a [mixed strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixed_strategy) to derive a [solution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solution_concept) in game theory.
weak evolutionarily stable strategy (WESS) is a more broad form of [evolutionarily stable strategy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionarily_stable_strategy) (ESS).

Wealth maximization is a normative principle in [welfare economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_economics) that seeks to maximize the total “[economic surplus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_surplus)” in society by summing individuals’ [willingness to pay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willingness_to_pay) for desired goods, services, or states of affairs.

cost of business cycles is the decrease in [social welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_welfare), if any, caused by [business cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Business_cycle) fluctuations.

welfare definition of economics is an attempt by [Alfred Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Marshall), a pioneer of [neoclassical economics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassical_economics), to redefine his field of study.

Welfare dependency is the state in which a person or household is reliant on government [welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_spending) benefits for their income for a prolonged period of time, and without which they would not be able to meet the expenses of daily living.

Welfare economics is a field of economics that applies [microeconomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microeconomics) techniques to evaluate the overall [well-being](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well-being) (welfare) of a society.

welfarism is a theory that [well-being](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well-being), what is good for someone or what makes a life worth living, is the only thing that has [[Axiology#Intrinsic value|intrinsic value]].

Wellbeing economy is a [public policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_policy) framework in which the [economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy) is designed to serve social, health, cultural, equity and nature outcomes.
Wikiprogress is a defunct online platform for sharing information on the measurement of social, economic and environmental [progress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progress_(history)).

willingness to accept (WTA) is the minimum monetary amount that а person is willing to accept to sell a [good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goods) or [service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_(economics)), or to bear a [negative externality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negative_externality), such as pollution.

win–stay, lose–switch (also win–stay, lose–shift or Pavlov, named after [Ivan Pavlov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Pavlov)) is a [heuristic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heuristic) learning strategy used to model learning in decision situations.
Workfare is a governmental plan under which [welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welfare_spending) recipients are required to accept public-service jobs or to participate in job training.
working poor are working people whose incomes fall below a given [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line) due to low-income jobs and low familial household income.

Zermelo's theorem is a theorem about finite two-person games of [perfect information](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_information) in which the players move alternately and in which chance does not affect the decision making process.
zero-player game or no-player game is a [simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_simulation) game that has no [sentient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentience) players.
